stage_2_story.text_en:
Last Friday evening, Moshe sat down with his grandson Noam to watch Maccabi Tel Aviv play against Hapoel Beer Sheva in a big league match. Noam had his notebook ready to write down any new English football words he heard from the commentator.

The match started at a fast pace. In the tenth minute, Hapoel Beer Sheva's striker broke through the defence, but Maccabi's goalkeeper came racing off his line and made a superb save to keep the score level. Noam wrote down 'goalkeeper' in his notebook and showed it to Moshe.

Maccabi began to control the midfield. Their experienced midfielder kept the ball moving quickly from left to right, finding space for the wingers. In the thirty-second minute, Hapoel's defender brought down Maccabi's winger just outside the penalty area. The referee awarded a free kick. Maccabi's captain stepped up and curled the ball over the wall and into the net. One-nil!

Hapoel responded aggressively after the break. Their tall striker won nearly every header, and one of their defenders was shown a yellow card for a rough tackle from behind. Maccabi survived the pressure and hit back on the counter. In the seventy-fifth minute, Maccabi's striker completed a brilliant hat-trick — his third goal came from a corner kick, where he rose above two defenders and headed the ball into the bottom corner.

After the match, Noam counted ten new words in his notebook. Moshe smiled and said: 'If you keep watching football with me, your English will be excellent in no time.'
